groupedFindings.name: api communication
groupedFindings.detail: No client-side API communication detected (traditional_web)
groupedFindings.fix: Use environment-specific production builds (e.g., Angular environment.prod.ts without dev proxy.conf.json localhost URLs), enforce HTTPS for all API origins, require authentication on sensitive REST/GraphQL endpoints, remove secrets from public /assets/config.json files, and restrict allowed API origins via Content-Security-Policy connect-src and strict CORS policies.

meta.title: Client-Side API Communication & Endpoint Discovery
meta.plainExplanation: Inspects Single Page Application (SPA) HTML, JavaScript bundles (Angular, React, Vue, Next.js), runtime configuration files (/assets/config.json, /config.json, /env.js), and CSP connect-src directives to map client-to-API communication, discover backend REST/GraphQL/WebSocket endpoints, and detect unauthenticated API data exposure or insecure API configurations.
meta.whyItMatters: Modern SPAs communicate directly with same-origin or external backend APIs via Angular HttpClient, Fetch, Axios, or GraphQL. Hardcoded development/localhost API URLs, plaintext HTTP API endpoints on HTTPS pages, exposed runtime config files, or unauthenticated JSON API endpoints can leak sensitive customer data, credentials, and internal service topology.
meta.defaultFix: Use environment-specific production builds (e.g., Angular environment.prod.ts without dev proxy.conf.json localhost URLs), enforce HTTPS for all API origins, require authentication on sensitive REST/GraphQL endpoints, remove secrets from public /assets/config.json files, and restrict allowed API origins via Content-Security-Policy connect-src and strict CORS policies.
meta.remediation: Use environment-specific production builds (e.g., Angular environment.prod.ts without dev proxy.conf.json localhost URLs), enforce HTTPS for all API origins, require authentication on sensitive REST/GraphQL endpoints, remove secrets from public /assets/config.json files, and restrict allowed API origins via Content-Security-Policy connect-src and strict CORS policies.

meta.title: API BOLA / IDOR & Mass Assignment Privilege Attribute Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Inspects REST API object endpoints (/api/users/1) against a non-existent canary route to detect unauthenticated Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) and checks whether privilege-escalation fields (role, isAdmin, is_superuser) are exposed.
meta.whyItMatters: Broken Object Level Authorization (OWASP API1:2023) allows attackers to read or modify other users’ records by enumerating IDs, while Mass Assignment allows binding privileged fields like role or isAdmin.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce object-level ownership checks on every record lookup, use non-sequential UUIDs, and restrict request body deserialization to explicit allowlisted DTO fields.
meta.remediation: Enforce object-level ownership checks on every record lookup, use non-sequential UUIDs, and restrict request body deserialization to explicit allowlisted DTO fields.

meta.title: Web Cache Poisoning & Unkeyed Header Reflection (X-Forwarded-Host / X-Original-URL)
meta.plainExplanation: Probes an isolated cache-busted URL (?secscan_cb=<nonce>) with unkeyed forwarding headers (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Host, X-Original-URL) and performs a clean follow-up request to verify whether the reflected header is stored in a shared HTTP cache.
meta.whyItMatters: If a reverse proxy or CDN caches a response containing an unkeyed header value, an attacker can poison the shared cache and serve malicious scripts or redirects to all visitors.
meta.defaultFix: Include X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Scheme in the cache key (Vary header), or configure the web server and framework to ignore unauthenticated X-Forwarded-Host and X-Original-URL headers.
meta.remediation: Include X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Scheme in the cache key (Vary header), or configure the web server and framework to ignore unauthenticated X-Forwarded-Host and X-Original-URL headers.

groupedFindings.remediation: Include X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Scheme in the cache key (Vary header), or configure the web server and framework to ignore unauthenticated X-Forwarded-Host and X-Original-URL headers.

issues.issue: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors — iframe embedding possible

groupedFindings.detail: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors — iframe embedding possible
evidenceQuotes: HTTP 200 on /: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors — iframe embedding possible (XFO=missing)
groupedFindings.fix: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' (or SAMEORIGIN) and 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors none' (or 'self') headers to prevent unauthorized embedding in iframes.

meta.title: Clickjacking Protection

meta.whyItMatters: Attackers can trick users into clicking invisible buttons or submitting forms on your site while thinking they are on another site.
meta.defaultFix: Add the "X-Frame-Options: DENY" or "Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'" HTTP header.
meta.remediation: Add the "X-Frame-Options: DENY" or "Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'" HTTP header.

groupedFindings.title: Clickjacking Protection
groupedFindings.remediation: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' (or SAMEORIGIN) and 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors none' (or 'self') headers to prevent unauthorized embedding in iframes.

groupedFindings.detail: No CRLF response header injection detected.

meta.title: HTTP Response Splitting & CRLF Header Injection
meta.plainExplanation: Probes redirect and query parameters with URL-encoded CR/LF sequences (%0d%0aX-SecScan-Crlf: crlf9812injected) and verifies whether an actual X-SecScan-Crlf HTTP header is injected into the response headers.
meta.whyItMatters: When user input containing CR and LF characters is copied into an HTTP response header without newline stripping, attackers can inject arbitrary headers, set malicious cookies, or split the HTTP response body.
meta.defaultFix: Strip or reject CR (\r, %0d) and LF (\n, %0a) characters before writing any user-derived value into HTTP response headers.
meta.remediation: Strip or reject CR (\r, %0d) and LF (\n, %0a) characters before writing any user-derived value into HTTP response headers.

groupedFindings.title: HTTP Response Splitting & CRLF Header Injection
groupedFindings.remediation: Strip or reject CR (\r, %0d) and LF (\n, %0a) characters before writing any user-derived value into HTTP response headers.

meta.title: PHP, Laravel & Symfony Ecosystem CVEs (CVE-2025-1217, CVE-2025-27515, CVE-2024-50342 & Nov 2026 PHP CVEs)
meta.plainExplanation: Passively inspects X-Powered-By / Server PHP banners and exposed /composer.json and /composer.lock manifests for PHP core/FPM/CGI/session/stream CVEs (including CVE-2025-1217 and 12 November 2026 advisories), Laravel file validation bypass (CVE-2025-27515), and Symfony HttpFoundation Request parsing vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-50342).
meta.whyItMatters: Vulnerable PHP, Laravel, and Symfony versions can allow unauthenticated FastCGI request smuggling RCE, session deserialization/UAF RCE, uriparser integer overflows, cleartext TLS downgrades, HTTP DoS, uploaded file validation bypasses, and FPM status XSS.
meta.defaultFix: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.36+, 8.3.37+, 8.4.28+, 8.5.13+, or 8.6.0+ (or apply vendor distro security updates), upgrade laravel/framework to 11.44.1+ or 12.1.1+, and upgrade symfony/http-foundation to 6.4.14+ or 7.1.7+. Remove composer.json/composer.lock from public web roots and set expose_php = Off.
meta.remediation: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.36+, 8.3.37+, 8.4.28+, 8.5.13+, or 8.6.0+ (or apply vendor distro security updates), upgrade laravel/framework to 11.44.1+ or 12.1.1+, and upgrade symfony/http-foundation to 6.4.14+ or 7.1.7+. Remove composer.json/composer.lock from public web roots and set expose_php = Off.

meta.title: Smart TV, IP Camera, PC/Workstation & Network Device Security Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Performs non-intrusive discovery and security auditing across Smart TVs (Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, Roku ECP, Google TV / Android TV / Chromecast, Sony Bravia, Vizio SmartCast, Philips JointSpace, Apple AirPlay, DIAL), IP Cameras / NVRs (RTSP 554/8554, ONVIF SOAP, Hikvision ISAPI, Dahua, Axis, Xiongmai, UniFi Protect, unauthenticated snapshots), PCs / Workstations / Local Servers (Windows SMB/NetBIOS/MSRPC/RDP/WinRM/WSDAPI, macOS/Linux SSH/VNC/CUPS/NFS/AFP/rsync/mDNS, Docker TCP 2375, Ollama 11434, local dev servers, open shares), routers, printers, NAS, and IoT appliances.
meta.whyItMatters: Local network devices and workstations often expose unauthenticated REST/WebSocket control APIs, live RTSP/MJPEG camera feeds, cleartext admin UIs, unauthenticated Docker/Ollama/dev servers, or remote file-sharing and shell services (SMB 445, RDP 3389, WinRM 5985, ADB 5555, Telnet 23) that allow LAN attackers to hijack screens, view surveillance feeds, access files, or execute arbitrary commands.
meta.defaultFix: Segment Smart TVs, IP cameras/NVRs, and IoT appliances onto isolated VLANs with client isolation enabled. Require authentication and HTTPS/TLS on camera and appliance admin interfaces, enforce RTSP Digest auth, disable unused UPnP/DLNA/ADB/Telnet services, bind local dev servers, Docker, and Ollama to 127.0.0.1, and restrict SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH/VNC/NFS via host firewalls.
meta.remediation: Segment Smart TVs, IP cameras/NVRs, and IoT appliances onto isolated VLANs with client isolation enabled. Require authentication and HTTPS/TLS on camera and appliance admin interfaces, enforce RTSP Digest auth, disable unused UPnP/DLNA/ADB/Telnet services, bind local dev servers, Docker, and Ollama to 127.0.0.1, and restrict SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH/VNC/NFS via host firewalls.

groupedFindings.remediation: Segment Smart TVs, IP cameras/NVRs, and IoT appliances onto isolated VLANs with client isolation enabled. meta.title: DOM-Based XSS Source-to-Sink & Unsafe postMessage Listener Analysis
meta.plainExplanation: Inspects client-side JavaScript in HTML responses for direct untrusted DOM source-to-sink dataflows (location.hash / location.search flowing into innerHTML / document.write / eval) and window.addEventListener("message") handlers lacking event.origin validation.
meta.whyItMatters: DOM-based XSS executes entirely in the victim’s browser when client-side scripts pass attacker-controlled URL fragments or cross-window postMessage data directly into HTML/script execution sinks.
meta.defaultFix: Use textContent / innerText instead of innerHTML or document.write, sanitize dynamic HTML with DOMPurify, and always validate event.origin inside postMessage handlers.
meta.remediation: Use textContent / innerText instead of innerHTML or document.write, sanitize dynamic HTML with DOMPurify, and always validate event.origin inside postMessage handlers.

groupedFindings.title: DOM-Based XSS Source-to-Sink & Unsafe postMessage Listener Analysis
groupedFindings.remediation: Use textContent / innerText instead of innerHTML or document.write, sanitize dynamic HTML with DOMPurify, and always validate event.origin inside postMessage handlers.

groupedFindings.detail: Target HTTP transport routed via Source IP 104.21.78.35 (104.21.78.35:443); no origin WAF bypass or default vhost leakage detected.

meta.title: Direct Source-IP / Origin-IP HTTP Exposure & CDN/WAF Bypass
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies whether the target connects via a resolved or configured Source/Origin IP and checks if direct Source-IP HTTP/HTTPS requests bypass CDN/WAF edge protections or leak internal default virtual-host / origin server metadata.
meta.whyItMatters: When an origin server accepts direct HTTP/HTTPS connections on its Source IP outside the CDN/WAF IP allowlist, attackers can bypass edge WAF rules, rate limits, and bot protections by connecting directly to the Source IP.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict origin firewall ingress on ports 80/443 to trusted CDN/WAF IP ranges only, configure a default-deny catch-all virtual host (ssl_reject_handshake on; return 444;), and enforce Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS).
meta.remediation: Restrict origin firewall ingress on ports 80/443 to trusted CDN/WAF IP ranges only, configure a default-deny catch-all virtual host (ssl_reject_handshake on; return 444;), and enforce Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS).

meta.title: PHP session.upload_progress LFI-to-RCE & Serializer Mismatch (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619)
meta.plainExplanation: Passively and safely inspects PHP targets for the php2shell (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619) session.upload_progress multipart PHPSESSID fixation, raw filename session injection, var_destroy UAF, and FPM PS(serializer) handler mismatch conditions.
meta.whyItMatters: In PHP 5.4.0 through 8.5.11, the rfc1867 session.upload_progress handler accepts PHPSESSID from multipart POST form data ignoring session.use_only_cookies and writes raw filenames into session files, enabling LFI-to-RCE and deserialization RCE.
meta.defaultFix: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.35+, 8.3.36+, 8.4.27+, or 8.5.12+ (or 8.2.36+ / 8.3.37+ / 8.4.28+ / 8.5.13+), set session.upload_progress.enabled = Off, session.use_only_cookies = On, and enforce session.serialize_handler = php_serialize.
meta.remediation: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.35+, 8.3.36+, 8.4.27+, or 8.5.12+ (or 8.2.36+ / 8.3.37+ / 8.4.28+ / 8.5.13+), set session.upload_progress.enabled = Off, session.use_only_cookies = On, and enforce session.serialize_handler = php_serialize.

groupedFindings.title: PHP session.upload_progress LFI-to-RCE & Serializer Mismatch (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619)
groupedFindings.remediation: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.35+, 8.3.36+, 8.4.27+, or 8.5.12+ (or 8.2.36+ / 8.3.37+ / 8.4.28+ / 8.5.13+), set session.upload_progress.enabled = Off, session.use_only_cookies = On, and enforce session.serialize_handler = php_serialize.

meta.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) URL Parameter & Backend Fetcher Surface
meta.plainExplanation: Tests URL/webhook/callback query parameters (?url=, ?webhook=, ?uri=) with a non-routable RFC 2606 domain (http://secscan-ssrf-probe.invalid/) to detect whether the backend server attempts an outbound HTTP fetch and leaks HTTP client connection errors.
meta.whyItMatters: Unvalidated server-side URL fetchers allow attackers to pivot into internal VPC networks, query cloud instance metadata services (169.254.169.254), and scan internal ports.
meta.defaultFix: Validate user-supplied URLs against a strict domain allowlist, connect directly to the validated IP (PinnedDialer), and block all RFC1918, loopback, link-local, and cloud metadata IP ranges.
meta.remediation: Validate user-supplied URLs against a strict domain allowlist, connect directly to the validated IP (PinnedDialer), and block all RFC1918, loopback, link-local, and cloud metadata IP ranges.

meta.title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI — Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker, EL, ERB, EJS)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests URL query parameters with non-destructive arithmetic template expressions across Jinja2/Twig/Pebble ({{7919*13}}), Freemarker/Spring EL/Thymeleaf (${7919*13}), and ERB/EJS (<%= 7919*13 %>), verifying that the server evaluates the expression to 102947 without reflecting the un-evaluated formula.
meta.whyItMatters: When user input is concatenated directly into a server-side template string before rendering, attackers can execute arbitrary template expressions and achieve remote code execution (RCE).
meta.defaultFix: Never pass user-supplied strings as template source code. Always pass user data as named context variables into pre-compiled static templates.
meta.remediation: Never pass user-supplied strings as template source code. Always pass user data as named context variables into pre-compiled static templates.

groupedFindings.title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI — Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker, EL, ERB, EJS)
groupedFindings.remediation: Never pass user-supplied strings as template source code. Always pass user data as named context variables into pre-compiled static templates.

meta.plainExplanation: Inspects REST API object endpoints (/api/users/1) against a non-existent canary route to detect unauthenticated Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) and checks whether privilege-escalation fields (role, isAdmin, is_superuser) are exposed.

meta.title: Web Cache Poisoning & Unkeyed Header Reflection (X-Forwarded-Host / X-Original-URL)
meta.plainExplanation: Probes an isolated cache-busted URL (?secscan_cb=<nonce>) with unkeyed forwarding headers (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Host, X-Original-URL) and performs a clean follow-up request to verify whether the reflected header is stored in a shared HTTP cache.
meta.whyItMatters: If a reverse proxy or CDN caches a response containing an unkeyed header value, an attacker can poison the shared cache and serve malicious scripts or redirects to all visitors.
meta.defaultFix: Include X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Scheme in the cache key (Vary header), or configure the web server and framework to ignore unauthenticated X-Forwarded-Host and X-Original-URL headers.
meta.remediation: Include X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Scheme in the cache key (Vary header), or configure the web server and framework to ignore unauthenticated X-Forwarded-Host and X-Original-URL headers.

meta.title: Smart TV, IP Camera, PC/Workstation & Network Device Security Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Performs non-intrusive discovery and security auditing across Smart TVs (Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, Roku ECP, Google TV / Android TV / Chromecast, Sony Bravia, Vizio SmartCast, Philips JointSpace, Apple AirPlay, DIAL), IP Cameras / NVRs (RTSP 554/8554, ONVIF SOAP, Hikvision ISAPI, Dahua, Axis, Xiongmai, UniFi Protect, unauthenticated snapshots), PCs / Workstations / Local Servers (Windows SMB/NetBIOS/MSRPC/RDP/WinRM/WSDAPI, macOS/Linux SSH/VNC/CUPS/NFS/AFP/rsync/mDNS, Docker TCP 2375, Ollama 11434, local dev servers, open shares), routers, printers, NAS, and IoT appliances.
meta.whyItMatters: Local network devices and workstations often expose unauthenticated REST/WebSocket control APIs, live RTSP/MJPEG camera feeds, cleartext admin UIs, unauthenticated Docker/Ollama/dev servers, or remote file-sharing and shell services (SMB 445, RDP 3389, WinRM 5985, ADB 5555, Telnet 23) that allow LAN attackers to hijack screens, view surveillance feeds, access files, or execute arbitrary commands.
meta.defaultFix: Segment Smart TVs, IP cameras/NVRs, and IoT appliances onto isolated VLANs with client isolation enabled. Require authentication and HTTPS/TLS on camera and appliance admin interfaces, enforce RTSP Digest auth, disable unused UPnP/DLNA/ADB/Telnet services, bind local dev servers, Docker, and Ollama to 127.0.0.1, and restrict SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH/VNC/NFS via host firewalls.
meta.remediation: Segment Smart TVs, IP cameras/NVRs, and IoT appliances onto isolated VLANs with client isolation enabled. Require authentication and HTTPS/TLS on camera and appliance admin interfaces, enforce RTSP Digest auth, disable unused UPnP/DLNA/ADB/Telnet services, bind local dev servers, Docker, and Ollama to 127.0.0.1, and restrict SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH/VNC/NFS via host firewalls.

meta.remediation: Restrict origin firewall ingress on ports 80/443 to trusted CDN/WAF IP ranges only, configure a default-deny catch-all virtual host (ssl_reject_handshake on; return 444;), and enforce Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS).

meta.title: PHP session.upload_progress LFI-to-RCE & Serializer Mismatch (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619)
meta.plainExplanation: Passively and safely inspects PHP targets for the php2shell (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619) session.upload_progress multipart PHPSESSID fixation, raw filename session injection, var_destroy UAF, and FPM PS(serializer) handler mismatch conditions.
meta.whyItMatters: In PHP 5.4.0 through 8.5.11, the rfc1867 session.upload_progress handler accepts PHPSESSID from multipart POST form data ignoring session.use_only_cookies and writes raw filenames into session files, enabling LFI-to-RCE and deserialization RCE.
meta.defaultFix: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.35+, 8.3.36+, 8.4.27+, or 8.5.12+ (or 8.2.36+ / 8.3.37+ / 8.4.28+ / 8.5.13+), set session.upload_progress.enabled = Off, session.use_only_cookies = On, and enforce session.serialize_handler = php_serialize.
meta.remediation: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.35+, 8.3.36+, 8.4.27+, or 8.5.12+ (or 8.2.36+ / 8.3.37+ / 8.4.28+ / 8.5.13+), set session.upload_progress.enabled = Off, session.use_only_cookies = On, and enforce session.serialize_handler = php_serialize.

findings.detail: No SSRF backend URL-fetcher surface detected.

meta.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) URL Parameter & Backend Fetcher Surface
meta.plainExplanation: Tests URL/webhook/callback query parameters (?url=, ?webhook=, ?uri=) with a non-routable RFC 2606 domain (http://secscan-ssrf-probe.invalid/) to detect whether the backend server attempts an outbound HTTP fetch and leaks HTTP client connection errors.
meta.whyItMatters: Unvalidated server-side URL fetchers allow attackers to pivot into internal VPC networks, query cloud instance metadata services (169.254.169.254), and scan internal ports.
meta.defaultFix: Validate user-supplied URLs against a strict domain allowlist, connect directly to the validated IP (PinnedDialer), and block all RFC1918, loopback, link-local, and cloud metadata IP ranges.
meta.remediation: Validate user-supplied URLs against a strict domain allowlist, connect directly to the validated IP (PinnedDialer), and block all RFC1918, loopback, link-local, and cloud metadata IP ranges.

meta.title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI — Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker, EL, ERB, EJS)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests URL query parameters with non-destructive arithmetic template expressions across Jinja2/Twig/Pebble ({{7919*13}}), Freemarker/Spring EL/Thymeleaf (${7919*13}), and ERB/EJS (<%= 7919*13 %>), verifying that the server evaluates the expression to 102947 without reflecting the un-evaluated formula.
meta.whyItMatters: When user input is concatenated directly into a server-side template string before rendering, attackers can execute arbitrary template expressions and achieve remote code execution (RCE).
meta.defaultFix: Never pass user-supplied strings as template source code. Always pass user data as named context variables into pre-compiled static templates.
meta.remediation: Never pass user-supplied strings as template source code. Always pass user data as named context variables into pre-compiled static templates.

findings.title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI — Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker, EL, ERB, EJS)
findings.remediation: Never pass user-supplied strings as template source code. Always pass user data as named context variables into pre-compiled static templates.

meta.remediation: Remove dangling CNAME, A, and AAAA DNS records before deprovisioning cloud buckets or PaaS applications.

meta.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).

meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

findings.title: PHP Local File Inclusion (LFI)
findings.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).

meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
meta.remediation: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.
